summary: Robocurve, in San Francisco per the YC page, tests how well AI models control real robots and publishes the results. It describes itself as an independent third-party evaluator and says it is incorporated as a Public Benefit Corporation. It maintains Inspect Robots, an MIT-licensed evaluation framework that lists packages for several commercial robot platforms.
oneLiner: Tests how well AI models control real robots and publishes the results
thesis: If general-purpose robot policies keep improving, buyers, labs and regulators will need third-party measurement on real hardware. Robocurve is an early attempt to be that reference. It could give investors comparable performance data on models portfolio companies depend on.
stage: Seed stage. The company blog announced a $10M seed round on 14 September 2026, led by Initialized Capital with Notable Capital, Decasonic, Y Combinator, Halcyon Futures and "many others". No valuation is given. An EDGAR full-text search on 2 October 2026 returned nothing for Robocurve. YC lists the Summer 2026 batch. The seed post dates incorporation to about three months before 14 September.

team.name: Jay Chooi
team.background: Founder and CEO per the YC page. It lists a Harvard MA in Statistics, a Rhodes Scholarship and research at the UK AI Security Institute.

team.name: Aris Zhu
team.background: Former co-founder (X bio reads "prev cofounder @robocurve"). YC partner Ankit Gupta's article lists Harvard's Computational Robotics Lab, Amazon Robotics, Amazon's AGI Lab and Yondu Robotics.

team.name: Edward Sun
team.background: Member of Technical Staff per the NBC News video description of 23 September 2026. No source opened states prior background.

questions: The pages opened disclose no price, contract or paying customer. What is revenue to date and who are the first paying counterparties?
When and why did Aris Zhu, presented as co-founder in July 2026, leave? What happened to the founder equity, and who now leads robotics hardware?
How does the charter define independence if evaluated labs are also customers, and do OpenAI or Anthropic have any role in reports on subdomains named after them?
Inspect Robots is MIT-licensed. What stops a lab, a university consortium or an existing evaluator such as METR from running the same benchmarks, and what is proprietary?
risks: No disclosed revenue model or customer. The framework is MIT-licensed and reports are published openly, so it may behave more like a research institute than a venture-scale business.
Co-founder change within about three months of incorporation. Aris Zhu now lists the role as previous on X, YC shows a single active founder, and no source opened explains why.
Independence and revenue may conflict if payers are the labs and robot makers being scored. Reports on OpenAI and Anthropic models sit on subdomains named after those labs.
unverified: The company says Inspect Robots has 97k+ downloads, not reproduced. Pypistats shows 49,756 for the inspect-robots package including mirrors, 7 July to 1 October 2026.
The company reports 6M+ research views and sign-ups from 200+ institutions, not independently confirmed.
When and why Aris Zhu left is not stated in any source opened.

announcement.what: Aris Zhu, then a co-founder, posted on LinkedIn that Zhu and Jay Chooi were in Y Combinator's Summer 2026 batch building Robocurve.
